edition.alertText: Iran claims 7 tankers hit overnight — largest single-day toll since war began; Brent surges to $113 (5-month high); Houthis strike Dammam airport killing 2; Aramco Dhahran HQ evacuated; E3 + R4 foreign ministers meet in Istanbul today

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 237 with Iran claiming the largest single-day attack on shipping since the war began. On October 22, Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said seven tankers were hit overnight — four caught fire while conducting ship-to-ship oil transfers, and three were disabled after striking naval mines. Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 28 attacks on ships in October alone, the highest monthly toll since the conflict began on February 28. UKMTO has now recorded 153 incidents since March 1, though the agency acknowledged it is struggling to capture the full picture as many operators refuse to report attacks. Despite the surge in attacks, oil continues to flow: Kpler data shows total Middle East oil exports averaging 24.6 million barrels per day — above the 23.3 million bpd pre-war baseline — driven by Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which Aramco says has ramped from 2 million to 7 million barrels per day, bypassing Hormuz entirely. CENTCOM marked 100 days of its reinstated blockade of Iranian ports, claiming it has prevented $25 billion in Iranian crude exports, and Kpler reported that Iran's shadow fleet tankers have run out of oil to sell to China.

Oil markets surged on Thursday as Brent crude jumped roughly 4% to $113.17 per barrel — its highest close since May — while WTI briefly crossed $100 before settling at $99.19, driven by the 7-tanker attack claims, Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, and Aramco's reported evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters. In early Asian trade Friday, Brent eased to $112.96 (down 0.19%) and WTI dipped to $98.12 (down 0.27%), with prices set for a third straight weekly gain. Gold held steady near $4,128 per ounce amid safe-haven demand. VLCC tanker rates remain at record levels near $1.4 million per day for Gulf-to-East Asia routes, with freight adding $33–41 per barrel to delivered crude cost. QatarEnergy signed a landmark deal with Cheniere to buy 4 million tonnes per year of US LNG through 2054, its first American offtake agreement — a stark admission that its own Hormuz-dependent exports remain crippled. Dutch TTF gas surged to nearly €90 per megawatt-hour, and Japan's April–September trade deficit nearly doubled to ¥2.82 trillion ($17.8 billion) on higher oil and LNG costs. US diesel remains above $6.31 per gallon.

Geopolitical tensions widened sharply as the war's toll spread beyond the strait. The Houthis claimed four attacks inside Saudi Arabia over 48 hours, including on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam (2 killed, 8 injured — death toll up from 1), a Defense Ministry building in Riyadh, and airports in Abha. Aramco reportedly told staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters after Houthi strikes, while the Saudi-led coalition intercepted drones over Riyadh and Medina. Trump accused Iran of making up strikes to drive up oil prices before the midterms, writing that Iran is 'doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil,' while CENTCOM dismissed Iran's mine claims. NPR reported the US and Israel are planning possible post-midterm strikes on Iran, including targeting Pickaxe Mountain. Foreign ministers from the E3 (UK, France, Germany) and the R4 (Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt) are meeting in Istanbul on Friday to discuss Yemen, Hormuz, and a path to de-escalation. On the supply chain front, S&P Global warned that Hormuz energy shocks combined with an emerging El Niño could trigger a global food crisis, with sulphur exports down 39% and Brazil's corn forecast cut by 6 million tonnes. Italian truckers and farmers blocked refineries over record diesel prices, leaving shelves and petrol stations empty in southern Italy.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased to ~$810/tonne by end-September from $1,000+ peak but remain far above pre-war levels. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 due to sulfur shortage. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Only 8 urea vessels left Gulf waters in September. ~850kt urea stranded across Iran and Arabian Gulf by mid-July (ICIS). 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). S&P Global warns Hormuz + El Niño = global food crisis; Brazil corn forecast cut 6M tonnes. Italian farmers blocking refineries over diesel.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports still crippled — QatarEnergy signs historic deal to buy 4M tonnes/yr US LNG from Cheniere through 2054. Dutch TTF gas near €90/MWh. Japan's trade deficit doubled to ¥2.82T ($17.8B) on higher energy costs. JERA CEO says Qatar supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
